plan.change: Phase C follow-up: harden failure-path diagnostics in trusted Change OS workflows
expectedChanges: Escape candidate-controlled content in Plan Lock, Scope, Risk, and Impact CLI failure diagnostics while preserving raw machine values internally.
Escape Risk human-detail rendering through the shared human-text boundary.
Remove raw candidate path and Plan base values from trusted workflow shell diagnostics and make inline Plan Lock parse failures fixed-text.
Add regressions for invalid-Plan diagnostics and workflow failure-path logging.
hqDecisions: This package addresses only the final C3-1 closure-audit finding: candidate-controlled text can still reach trusted operator logs through failure-path diagnostics.
Reuse the shared escapeHumanText display boundary; do not mutate Plan values, validation errors, machine JSON evidence, gate decisions, exit codes, schemas, or artifact contents.
PR Gate and Change Verification must apply the same failure-path display contract.
rulesApplied: C3-1 final closure audit failure-path finding
plan.manualCheckExemptionReason: Change OS diagnostics hardening only; covered by deterministic CLI/workflow regressions, trusted PR checks, Codex review, and invalid-Plan post-merge canary.
plan.rollback: Revert this staging-only diagnostics hardening PR; production remains untouched.
outOfScope: Phase E semantic scope and concurrency controls
unverified: An invalid-Plan failure canary and a final clean closure audit remain required before C3-1 is formally closed.
plan.problem: Trusted success-path human formatters are escaped, but invalid Plan and other failure diagnostics can still include candidate-controlled strings. PR Gate prints CLI stderr directly, Change Verification reprints captured stderr, and both workflows contain shell diagnostics that can echo arbitrary changed paths or unvalidated Plan base values.
plan.currentContract: Scope and Impact human reports use escapeHumanText, machine JSON remains literal, raw JSON is suppressed from Verification logs, but CLI catch/Plan Lock errors and several workflow shell failure messages still expose raw candidate-controlled content.
plan.whyExistingIsInsufficient: A malicious invalid Plan or unusual failure-path filename can inject newline or bidi controls into operator-visible trusted logs even though mechanical gate decisions remain correct.
plan.design: Use escapeHumanText only when emitting CLI stderr or human Risk details; keep internal errors and machine reports literal. Replace workflow shell diagnostics that include arbitrary candidate values with fixed messages, and make inline Plan Lock JSON parse diagnostics fixed-text. Preserve all gate and evidence semantics.
alternativesRejected: Reject all control characters in Plan content; display escaping preserves legitimate content and keeps machine evidence exact.
Sanitize validation data at source; that would alter machine semantics instead of only display semantics.
Suppress all failure diagnostics; fixed or escaped diagnostics retain useful operational signal without exposing raw candidate text.
plan.compatibility: Exit codes, validation rules, JSON reports, Plan Lock digest semantics, evidence schemas, artifact naming, and required checks remain unchanged. Only operator-visible diagnostics are escaped or fixed.
boundaryCases: Invalid authority/class/path values containing newline and bidi controls render as visible escape sequences on one physical line.
Plan Lock INVALID output preserves one bullet per validation error without raw embedded controls.
Risk human details remain readable and cannot introduce extra physical status lines.
Unexpected lock-commit paths and unvalidated locked baseSha values are not echoed raw by either trusted workflow.
Machine gate-error evidence may retain literal stderr semantics while operator logs receive only escaped stderr.
testPlan: Add CLI regressions for Plan Lock, Scope, Risk, and Impact invalid Plan diagnostics with newline plus bidi controls.
Assert Risk human details use escapeHumanText.
Assert both trusted workflows do not echo raw unexpected paths or locked Plan base values and inline Plan Lock parse errors are fixed-text.
Run Change Operations Tests, Change PR Gate, and Change Verification Evidence on the exact PR head and request Codex adversarial review.
After merge, run an invalid-Plan failure canary with malicious diagnostic text, inspect both trusted workflow logs, then run a valid final canary if needed and repeat closure audit.
plan.promotionRisk: Staging Change OS only. A mistake could hide diagnostics or alter gate behavior, so exact-head required checks, adversarial review, and a post-merge invalid-Plan canary are mandatory.
